prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: self-employed income evidence. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a self-employed applicant provides the latest SA302s and corresponding HMRC tax year overviews, I can usually reconcile income more quickly; when the figures differ, I pause until the mismatch is explained."},{"type":"fact","content":"When trading accounts are prepared by a qualified accountant, I treat them as stronger evidence if they are signed, dated and cover the right business period, especially where the applicant has fluctuating earnings."},{"type":"observation","content":"When an applicant has multiple income streams from self-employment, I check each source separately rather than assuming they should be averaged together, because some streams are too irregular to rely on."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the business is newly established, I prefer to see at least two years of evidence unless there is a clear, well-supported reason to accept a shorter track record."},{"type":"observation","content":"When business expenses are unusually high, I look closely at whether the declared profit is a better indicator of affordability than turnover, as gross receipts alone can be misleading."},{"type":"fact","content":"When using retained profits from a limited company, I need clear evidence that the applicant controls those funds and that they are genuinely available for personal use, not just shown on paper."},{"type":"observation","content":"When income has fallen in the most recent year, I do not rely on the best historic year alone; I look for a sensible trend and ask whether the lower figure is likely to continue."},{"type":"preference","content":"When bank statements are used to support self-employed income, I prefer them to tie back neatly to declared accounts and tax documents, rather than standing in isolation."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a sole trader’s income is seasonal, I make sure the evidence covers a full cycle so I do not overstate affordability by taking a strong trading month at face value."},{"type":"fact","content":"When tax returns are not yet available for the latest year, I can sometimes proceed with management accounts or interim figures, but only if they are recent, credible and supported by a clear explanation."}]}
